absent: Full structure layouts with field order, sizes, offsets and padding for xarray, idr, ida and radix tree types.
Numeric values of flags, marks, tags, chunk parameters, error codes and header selectors.
Locking and calling context requirements for identifier and tree operations outside the shown interrupt saving region.
Memory ordering, lifetime and concurrency guarantees for protected traversal beyond observed publication and deferred free usage.
Allocation failure, growth limits and performance behavior outside the shown retry and exhaustion paths.
Detailed formatting edge behavior for zero length input and exact buffer thresholds beyond the reported requirement rule.
Ownership and behavior of cross dossier helpers listed as stubs.

findings.text: Provides a single line hexadecimal renderer for caller memory that writes grouped digit text plus an optional human readable suffix into a caller supplied buffer and reports the length produced or the length that would have been required.
Provides a multi line diagnostic emitter that divides a caller range into rows, renders each row with the single line renderer, and writes one log record per row with a caller chosen header style.
Provides side effect free population count helpers for several input widths that return the number of set bits present in the given value.

Provides identifier allocation with remembered position and wrap around retry for one family and bounded least free bit allocation inside a caller range for another family, returning a numeric identifier or a negative failure indication.

Provides identifier space access through callback iteration over present entries, forward cursor based lookup of the next present entry, and replacement of a stored pointer with return of the prior value or a missing entry indication.
Provides a tag membership predicate for an index that first consults aggregated root state and range coverage and then follows internal levels only while each visited level claims the tag.

Provides cursor based extended array access to fetch the entry addressed by a cursor, install or clear entries with occupancy and mark maintenance, recover from allocation shortage using a spare node, and release spare resources.

Dump geometry normalizes unsupported row sizes to a default, limits one formatting call to one row, coerces unsupported or misaligned grouping to single byte groups, derives group count and suffix column placement from effective sizes, and separates plain digit output from padded output with printable rendering.

Population count behavior depends only on bits within the stated width, preserves results across fast multiplier and portable algorithmic variants, and builds wider counts from narrower counts according to native word size.

Identifier values combine a stored offset with a configurable base, clamp open ended maxima to the largest signed value, reject negative minima, treat nonpositive maxima as unbounded before clamping, and advance a stored next hint after successful cyclic allocation.

Cursor addressing derives per level offsets from index bits shifted by node depth and masked to chunk width, maps out of range indexes to a bounded empty outcome, follows sibling redirection during descent, and extends lookup maxima to cover multi slot spans.

Mark state is maintained per slot with aggregated summaries toward the root and array flags, bulk initialization on fresh nodes when free tracking is active, consolidation of spanned slots onto a canonical position, and ordering that clears marks before an entry becomes empty.

Range bit allocation holds an interrupt saving cursor lock while searching and updating the underlying array and releases it on all paths including exhaustion, with memory allocation and shortage recovery performed after release before any retry.

Tree updates publish slot changes with ordering suitable for concurrent readers and reclaim nodes only after a grace period, with reclaimed storage cleared and housekeeping reinitialized before return to the slab allocator.

Cursor state associates a target array with an index and span, a located node and offset, a spare node for recovery, an update hook and reclamation context, and error or boundary indication; nodes associate shift and offset with occupancy counts, parent linkage, owning array, slot storage, mark storage, housekeeping linkage and deferred free linkage; arrays associate a head pointer with a flag word.

One identifier structure associates a next hint with a base and an underlying tree; another associates an extended array with bitmap chunks addressed by chunk number and bit offset; tree nodes associate slot storage with tag storage, housekeeping linkage and deferred free linkage.

Cursor operation distinguishes located, bounded empty, invalid, error and restart request conditions, where erroneous or invalid conditions produce empty loads and suppress creation, bounded conditions persist until repositioning, and shortage recovery can request a restart once a spare node is available.

Tree topology evolves through root expansion and demand node insertion with linkage and accounting updates, followed by slot clearing, empty chain collapse, single entry root shrinking with zero entry normalization, and deferred reclamation of removed nodes.

Bounded bit allocation moves among searching free marked chunks, consuming inline values or bitmap chunks or empty positions, and terminating in success, range exhaustion, or temporary release followed by allocation and retry with disposal of unneeded spares.

Diagnostic emission entry receives severity, prefix text, header selector, geometry, source range and printable control, normalizes geometry, and produces one log record per row with storage sized for the largest supported row.

Callback iteration entry receives an identifier structure, a function invoked with numeric identifier plus stored pointer plus caller data, and opaque caller context, halting early and propagating the first nonzero callback result.

Insufficient destination space truncates rendering yet preserves termination whenever any space exists; the reported requirement differs between printable and plain modes, so callers must derive sizing from the return value rather than assuming completion.

Removed or collapsed storage is marked for retry, occupancy is checked against chunk capacity, root removal resets cursor position to a boundary condition, and identifier iteration guards against values beyond the signed maximum.

Dump interface facts include supported row widths 16 and 32 with default 16, supported group widths that are powers of two through 8 with fallback 1, and distinct header selector behaviors for address and offset plus a default plain behavior.

Array and identifier interface facts include chunk size with mask and shift derivation, multi slot span sizing, bitmap granularity for range allocation, signed maximum identifier ceiling, free mark tracking with mark ceiling, and distinct indications for exhaustion, missing entry and memory shortage.
